item.title: Elon Musk-backed super PAC spends $800,000 to back GOP midterm candidates
item.description: Elon Musk's super PAC disclosed over $800,000 in spending last month to support Republican Senate and House candidates in competitive races, with the bulk in Texas and Maine.

item.title: Military personnel told last month to stop calling Iran conflict "Operation Epic Fury"
item.description: The Pentagon says "Operation Epic Fury" ended on May 5, after an Air Force email last month told service members to stop using the name for ongoing Iran operations.

item.title: 2 killed, at least 5 others injured in downtown Minneapolis shooting
item.description: Two people are dead and at least five others are injured, including three officers, after a shooting near 15 East Grant Street Wednesday afternoon in downtown Minneapolis, according to police. The suspected shooter is also dead.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy jury deadlocked, ends day without verdict
item.description: The jury in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial, which signaled Wednesday for a second straight day it is deadlocked, left without a verdict and will resume deliberations on Thursday.

item.title: Trump says U.S. prepared to hit Iran "anytime we want" after "very heavy attack"
item.description: The U.S. military was looking into Iran's allegations that people at a wedding party were killed in the American strikes, a spokesman said.

item.title: Judge blocks Trump's latest effort to narrow birthright citizenship
item.description: A federal judge has temporarily blocked a Trump executive order that would prevent certain people from automatically becoming U.S. citizens at birth.

item.title: 2 killed, multiple injured and gunman dead after mass shooting in downtown Minneapolis
item.description: Minneapolis police say they are responding to a deadly shooting that killed two people and injured multiple others, including police officers, law enforcement sources say. The shooter is also dead. CBS News correspondent Jonah Kaplan reports.

item.title: Malta businessman found not guilty in car bomb killing of journalist
item.description: Daphne Caruana Galizia's killing shocked Europe, led to protests that toppled a prime minister and exposed a culture of impunity in the European Union's smallest state.

item.title: At least 1 killed, 6 injured in downtown Minneapolis shooting, hospital says
item.description: At least one person is dead and six others are injured after a shooting in downtown Minneapolis on Wednesday, the Hennepin County Medical Center says. CBS News Minnesota's Conor Wight reports. Then, CBS News' Jonah Kaplan joins with more.

item.title: Retired Navy veteran reclaims title of oldest person to finish crossing Appalachian Trail
item.description: A retired Navy veteran set a record as the oldest person to ever finish hiking along the 2,200-mile-long Appalachian Trail in 2017. After a friend took his title in 2021, Dale Sanders reclaimed it this week. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: Pentagon rolls out guidelines to test service members for testosterone
item.description: The Pentagon will begin requiring male service members ages 30 and older to get screened for testosterone deficiency, after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth called for the change over the summer.

item.title: Expert questions legality of U.S. strikes on alleged drug boats as death toll hits 227
item.description: Brian Finucane, senior adviser for the U.S. program at the International Crisis Group, joins "The Daily Report" to analyze the Trump administration's deadly campaign against alleged drug-smuggling boats.

item.title: Police find bobcat in 93-year-old woman's home near Seattle
item.description: When a 93-year-old woman near Seattle heard strange noises in her house last month, she called the cops to report a prowler. Police found an unexpected intruder - a bobcat. Carter Evans has the story.

item.title: New York City bans AI in elementary and middle schools
item.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced a 1-year moratorium on the use of AI in elementary and middle school classrooms on Wednesday. Danielle Giunta, first deputy chancellor of NYC public schools, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: Preserving the stories and voices of 9/11 | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: 60 Minutes examines the profound challenges of constructing the 9/11 Museum and its mission to memorialize the attack and remember the voices and faces of the victims and first responders.

item.title: Trump says U.S. issued a "very heavy attack," on Iran and is "prepared to do another one anytime"
item.description: Oil prices jumped higher on Wednesday after the U.S. and Iran traded military strikes, and gas prices are on track to hit a Labor Day weekend high. Charlie D'Agata reports on the attacks.

item.title: Iran accuses U.S. of war crime after strike allegedly kills at least 4 at wedding
item.description: Iran accused the United States of war crimes on Wednesday over a strike that they say killed multiple civilians at a wedding party near the Strait of Hormuz. CBS News' Weijia Jiang reports.

item.title: 9/2: CBS Evening News
item.description: Mass shooting in downtown Minneapolis; jurors were deadlocked for the second time in the Lindsay Clancy trial.

item.title: Democratic Rep. Tom Suozzi calls on party to reject DSA
item.description: As progressive and moderate Democrats debate the party's path forward, Rep. Tom Suozzi of New York is calling on fellow Democrats to reject the Democratic Socialists of America. Suozzi joins "The Takeout" to discuss his piece in The Free Press, a Paramount publication.

item.title: Gina Hinojosa calls Abbott's Texas data center pause "an attempt to protect his reelection chances"
item.description: The nationwide political debate over data centers has made its way into the Texas governor's race. Gov. Greg Abbott recently paused approvals for new data centers, but his Democratic opponent, State Rep. Gina Hinojosa, says she's skeptical he'll stick to it. Hinojosa joins "The Takeout" to discuss her campaign.

item.title: House rejects GOP effort to ban Supreme Court expansion in Constitution
item.description: A GOP-proposed constitutional amendment to limit the Supreme Court to nine justices failed in the House, coming up well short of the two-thirds majority needed.

item.title: $1 gold Trump coins are on sale, but they'll cost you more than $1 apiece
item.description: The U.S. Mint said the President Donald J. Trump $1 coin can be bought in packages of 25 for $61 or 100 coins for $154.50.

item.title: Meta says AI glasses fix stops users from secretly recording others
item.description: Meta upgrades its AI glasses' privacy features to block device users from filming people without their consent.

item.title: House votes to condemn socialism, with 8 Democrats joining Republicans
item.description: GOP leaders scheduled the vote after Democratic primary voters embraced a number of democratic socialist candidates.

item.title: Ex-Border Patrol commander Bovino was under investigation when he retired
item.description: CBP informed Gregory Bovino in an email on March 2 that the agency was "conducting an official Inquiry into allegations of misconduct reported to CBP." He initiated retirement 16 days later.

item.title: Lionel Richie hospitalized after weekend show
item.description: While performing in St. Louis on Saturday night, Lionel Richie appeared at one point to lean on a piano for support, according to video from the show.

item.title: How a duck helped a dog recover from panic attacks, medication that brought him down
item.description: Steve Hartman explores the unique bond between a family's duck and dog.

item.title: After a stranger gifts a boy with autism a piano, he dazzles the world: "He's Mozart level"
item.description: Back in 2023, a stranger gifted a boy with autism a piano after seeing his story on the local news. Now, the stranger is more like family, and the boy is dazzling the world with his music. Steve Hartman goes "On the Road" revisiting Jude's story.

item.title: How a man's daily routine of ordering gumbo wound up saving his life
item.description: At the Shrimp Basket restaurant in Pensacola, Florida, a customer consistently ordered a cup of gumbo for lunch and for dinner for 10 years. When he didn't show up one week, the chef went to his house to check on him. Steve Hartman goes "On the Road" with the story, months later.

item.title: How Boom Chicago launched Seth Meyers to "Saturday Night Live"
item.description: Seth Meyers said the Dutch improv theater Boom Chicago gave him and his comedy partner Jill Benjamin a "road map" to create a show that eventually got the attention of "Saturday Night Live."
